Native Claude picker experiment

Version-pinned, isolated experiment for Claude Desktop native reasoning metadata.

About 9 min read · 5 sections

On this page
01 Native Ultracode 02 Safety boundary 03 Run and verify 04 October 24 verification 05 October 25 desktop comparison

This is an experimental developer harness, not an installer or a supported Claude Desktop configuration. The normal adapter does not modify Claude.app. The experiment changes a disposable copy of Claude Desktop 2.42304.2 to teach its existing picker about explicitly declared opaque gateway models. It keeps one row per model and does not impersonate a Claude model family.

The native picker reads reasoning options from main-process model rows. Claude already generates a row for every configured gateway alias, but without thinking metadata for unknown IDs. Appending renderer rows does not fix that: the same-ID placeholders win. The trial fills only that main-process gap, before Claude's unchanged effort cap/default function. Explicit hybrid and signed catalog rows, existing thinking options, labels, permissions and capabilities are preserved. The renderer assets stay pristine.

The synthetic catalog has two models with different reasoning options. Fast is not enabled: this build explicitly marks claude_code_fast_mode as blocked_by_platform for third-party profiles. The experiment does not bypass that policy, even when a gateway model advertises priority service.

Native Ultracode

Eligible gateway routes can explicitly declare supports_ultracode: true in the trial catalog, together with xhigh reasoning. This adds Claude's special ultracode selector stop, not another model row and not an alias for ordinary Extra high reasoning. Routes without that opt-in or without xhigh do not receive the mode.

The native cap/default function is unchanged. Its result must still contain xhigh before the connector adds the separate Ultracode mode stop. Therefore a Low, Medium or High cap cannot expose Ultracode. Existing native, bundled, hybrid and verified catalog thinking descriptors remain authoritative.

The private trial CLI settings opt into enableWorkflows: true. Managed workflow restrictions and native availability checks still take precedence. The gateway does not execute agents or add orchestration policy: Claude's CLI owns Ultracode and tool execution.

The offline CLI smoke sends the same native control request used by the app: apply_flag_settings with effortLevel: "xhigh" and ultracode: true. It checks the get_settings.applied state, not just requested/effective configuration, then completes a synthetic Messages turn. Run it with an explicit native CLI:

node scripts/claude-native-trial/ultracode-smoke.mjs /absolute/path/to/native/claude

The test uses an empty private home and workspace, a generated fixture token, disabled nonessential traffic, and text-only synthetic model output. It denies tool permission requests and records only typed control/availability flags and reasoning metadata. It does not prove a real model's multi-agent fan-out quality.

The October 24, 2026 native CLI 2.1.299 run passed. Initialize, flag application and settings requests succeeded; applied reported effort: "xhigh", ultracode: true, ultracodeRequested: true and ultracodeAvailable: true for the opaque fixture route. The Messages request carried xhigh, and the CLI completed a successful result matching the synthetic marker. The sanitized Ultracode receipt records those checks without request or response content. A completed response is required: accepted configuration alone does not pass this smoke.

The native Ultracode menu click still needs an unlocked desktop. Neither this run nor the catalog tests claim that a real provider executed agent fan-out. This remains an isolated trial, not a change to the installed Claude app or the live MacBook profile.

Safety boundary

The source app must pass strict signature verification and match pinned hashes. The script only patches an already-created, owned app copy under a task-specific /tmp/claude-native-picker.<id> directory. It does not sign either app by default, change the bundle identifier, install startup jobs, or alter the installed app. The modified copy no longer has a valid resource seal. If macOS refuses to launch it, stop and obtain explicit permission before signing the isolated copy. With explicit owner approval, pass --adhoc-sign to the runner to re-sign only that copy for local testing. It preserves runtime and device/privacy entitlements and flags, but removes the three vendor-only application identifier, team identifier, and Keychain access-group claims that an ad-hoc signature cannot carry. The test uses synthetic credentials, not Anthropic Keychain identity. The runner verifies both signatures afterwards and records the local test signature. This is not a notarized distribution or a production install. Before sealing the bundles, the signer explicitly signs every confined Mach-O leaf (including .node modules and framework libraries). codesign --deep alone misses some libraries, which would retain a different Team ID and fail library validation at launch. An ad-hoc signature cannot satisfy this build's hardened library validation. To keep validation enabled, use --developer-id CERTIFICATE_SHA1 instead, with an existing Developer ID identity in the dedicated ~/Library/Keychains/apple-codesign.keychain-db. This does not create/import certificates, unlock a keychain, notarize, or publish anything. Do not disable library validation or system security as a shortcut.

A prelude redirects Electron app data, profile, logs, crash dumps, and the Code CLI configuration before vendor modules load. Cowork is disabled. The fixture uses an ephemeral loopback listener, a private generated credential, and synthetic text responses. Receipts contain only model IDs and sanitized reasoning/tier controls, never prompts, tools, or credentials. No provider subscription is used. The runner also disables app auto-updates in the trial profile, sets its working directory to the private empty workspace, and uses Chromium's --use-mock-keychain for synthetic Electron OSCrypt storage only. The mock key is not suitable for real credentials, does not isolate direct native Security framework integrations, and must never be used with a real profile. Do not connect Office365, sign in to provider accounts, or relaunch the trial without that flag. No real Keychain access should be approved for this experiment.

Run and verify

Create an APFS clone of the official app inside a new task-specific directory under /tmp, named Claude Native Trial.app. Do not use hard links. The trial runner expects the pinned official app at /Applications/Claude.app and the installed ~/.local/bin/gateway credential helper. Invoke:

node scripts/claude-native-trial/run.mjs /tmp/claude-native-picker.EXPLICIT_ID

Use the actual task directory, not the placeholder. A task directory can be used only once. Keep the runner alive during GUI testing; stop it with SIGINT when done. Check prepared.json, running.json, and requests.json in that directory. They are experimental receipts, not deployment readiness evidence.

On an unlocked desktop, verify that each opaque model appears exactly once, the available effort options match its declaration, selections survive model switching and continuation, and low/high/max reach /v1/messages as selected. Verify Standard/Fast separately, including refusal or hidden controls for an unsupported model. Never infer success from metadata or a screenshot alone. The harness does not enable remote debugging or bypass app security checks.

October 24 verification

On October 24, 2026, the owner explicitly approved re-signing the disposable copy. An ad-hoc signature first failed with restricted-entitlement error -424; after removing vendor identity claims it failed hardened library validation. The existing Developer ID identity, applied to every Mach-O leaf and then the bundles, allowed the trial process to stay running and create its own Electron and CLI state directories. Hardened runtime and library validation remain enabled. Both the original and trial app pass strict deep signature verification.

After the workstation was unlocked, the original launch was found waiting in an Electron Keychain read. It was stopped without approving access; the synthetic mock-Keychain launch opened the UI. An updater attempt had also used Claude's shared ShipIt cache before auto-updates were disabled in the trial. The installed app was not changed. A Finder automation request during folder selection was denied, not granted.

The corrected main-process hook displays Claude's own native Effort popover with its Faster-to-Smarter slider. A synthetic turn selected through that slider reached /v1/messages with output_config.effort: "low" and returned NATIVE_PICKER_OK. The bundled CLI executable ran under the private trial profile, and the selected project was the empty trial workspace. Native model menus contain exactly one row per fixture model. Defaults were separately observed as medium before the main hook; auxiliary requests can use high and are not evidence of a manual high-effort selection.

The cropped UI capture and sanitized receipt exclude unrelated desktop windows, credentials and prompts.

The workstation subsequently re-locked. Manual high/max forwarding, model-switch persistence and continued-session/relaunch checks are pending. This is not a deployed default or a MacBook rollout. A prior core run passed, but the latest full gate reported 3,303 passes, one failure and one skip: the untouched real-lsof idle-child test in service-claude-activity.test.ts failed. It also failed alone: this host's CoreDevice DeviceFS mount emits a can't stat() warning on lsof stderr. The service activity checker intentionally fails closed on incomplete process information. That check was not weakened. The final separate desktop suite, including Ultracode configuration and smoke regressions, reported 93 passes, no failures and one skip. Do not report the full gate as green. The synthetic runner and fixture were stopped after the workstation re-locked; the signed candidate and sanitized receipts remain for the pending tests.

October 25 desktop comparison

An isolated comparison on macbook-server exercised the actual Claude Desktop 2.42304.2 window with native CLI 2.1.299 and synthetic inference. The baseline copy had only the state-isolation prelude; its model-handling code and renderer matched the official app. The installed app, real profiles, accounts, and gateway service were not modified.

Experiment Observed result
Baseline claude-opus-5-5 row Native effort slider was visible, without an Ultracode stop.
/effort ultracode in the baseline chat Saved effort: xhigh and sessionSettings.ultracode: true; a follow-up completed with xhigh on the wire. The footer still showed Medium and the slider did not gain Ultracode.
Baseline opaque gateway row No native effort control was offered.
Existing metadata extension in the disposable copy The opaque row gained Claude's own Ultracode slider stop without a renderer change or a Claude-family identity.
Selecting that stop The session saved ultracode: true, the request retained the opaque model ID and xhigh, and the fixture reply completed.
Selecting Low afterward Cleared Ultracode, sent low, and completed another reply.
Quitting, relaunching, and reopening the same chat The Ultracode control remained selected; another reply completed at xhigh.
Lowering the opaque row's cap to High Removed Ultracode and limited the slider to Low, Medium, and High.

These observations supersede the assumption that /effort ultracode alone would make the baseline slider display the stop. They establish a working desktop control path in the disposable patched copy, not a production release.

A separate six-case CLI experiment used fresh homes and matched fixture model IDs for both claude-opus-5-5 and the opaque route. Both IDs reported active, available Ultracode and completed replies with Workflows unset or enabled. Setting enableWorkflows: false or disableWorkflows: true kept requested Ultracode inactive and unavailable. Accepted settings alone were not counted as active Ultracode. The 36 focused catalog, main-process, and CLI-smoke regression tests passed. Repository check and build also passed. The full test command stopped after 3,322 core passes, one skip, and the previously observed real-lsof idle-child failure on Studio. Its chained full desktop suite was therefore not reached; the 36 focused desktop tests were run separately.

The sanitized receipt, native control capture, and High-cap capture contain only fixture identity and generation controls. Real provider inference, actual Workflow agent fan-out, and production deployment remain unverified.

Run npm run check, npm run build, and npm test before handoff. Focused tests are in scripts/claude-desktop-tests/claude-native-*.test.mjs. Preserve required receipts and remove owned disposable staging after testing ends.
